column1: # BITWISE-PARITY 2026-08-15 (hermit-sabre): bitwise_parity IS A DETERMINISM ASSERT, NOT A CORRECTNESS ORACLE. PROVEN, THREE STEPS BRACKETED.

column2: SUBJECT: main's epoll_readiness.c, which is UNGATED on main (main() ends 'return 0;'). Mutation: printf reports 'ok - 3' instead of 'ok'.
STEP 0 mutation applied to SOURCE (not a silent no-op): yes, cmp differs.
STEP 1 ARTIFACT CHANGED (binaries differ): yes. Without this the acceptance would prove nothing.
STEP 2 valid : exit=0 verdict=matched bitwise_parity=True stdout='epoll ok=6'
STEP 2 mutant: exit=0 verdict=matched bitwise_parity=True stdout='epoll ok=3'  <-- ACCEPTED WHILE REPORTING HALF ITS CHECKS FAILED

MECHANISM FROM SOURCE, NOT INFERENCE. ci/test_harness.sh: a verify cell is gated by exactly two things -- 'status != 0 -> FAIL', and if asserted, assert_bitwise_parity_verdict reading the run's OWN verify-1.json.
observation_hash (test_harness.sh:2973) digests status+stdout+stderr, but in the single-run verify path the column is read into '_hash' AND DISCARDED (test_harness.sh:3784). It gates nothing there.
That digest is compared ONLY in multi-run paths (repeat_identical/chaos/stress), and there only against OTHER RUNS OF THE SAME BINARY. Still no external reference.
CONSEQUENCE: THE ONLY EXTERNAL ORACLE A verify CELL HAS IS ITS EXIT STATUS. bitwise_parity compares run1 to run2 of one binary, so a WRONG-BUT-CONSISTENT program is accepted by construction.
CENSUS -- AND IT REFINES THE ALARM RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT. Exactly 2 cells in the whole manifest tree carry assert = { bitwise_parity = true }:
backend-parity-c/set-tid-address (backend-parity-c.toml:84) -- EXIT-GATED since 61b9ba7aa, 'return ok == 4 ? 0 : 1;'
c-programs/pause-alarm-interrupt (c-programs.toml:3734) -- EXIT-GATED via early 'return 1;' failure paths

SO ZERO CELLS CURRENTLY RELY ON bitwise_parity AS THEIR ONLY GATE. THE INERT-COVERAGE TRAP IS A REAL MECHANISM WITH NO LIVE INSTANCE TODAY. The hazard is PROSPECTIVE: the assert reads as a correctness gate and is inert when paired with an ungated fixture.
61b9ba7aa IS THEREFORE CORRECTLY ORDERED, NOT OVERSCORED: its fixture half supplies the oracle and its comparator half adds determinism strictness. THE HAZARD IS COPYING ONLY THE COMPARATOR HALF.

PROPOSAL, NOT DEPLOYED: make the pairing structural -- manifest validation should REFUSE 'assert = { bitwise_parity = true }' on a cell whose fixture is not exit-gated. ci/manifest-plan already validates observation (main.rs:613), so this is one more rule in a shipping validator, NOT a new mechanism.
DO NOT RETIRE bitwise_parity. It is sound for what it measures. The defect is the INFERENCE that it discriminates correctness. Pair it with EXPECTED_CHECKS, which already ships.
CI-INFRASTRUCTURE CHANGE -> out-of-place clone protocol + owner. NOT implemented here.

column1: # DELTA-CHARACTERISED 2026-08-15 (hermit-sabre): THE ~799 EXTRA MESSAGES ARE IDENTIFIED. STILL NO CAUSE NAMED -- THIS IS WHAT THEY ARE, NOT WHY.

column2: METHOD: same fixture (uname-identity), hermit --log=info run --strict on each backend, compare the DETLOG stream.
log lines: ptrace 132, liteinst 982.   DETLOG records: ptrace 81, liteinst 817.
THE EXTRA MESSAGES ARE DETLOG SYSCALL RECORDS, AND THEY ARE DOMINATED BY ONE CALL:
read     ptrace 0   -> liteinst 468
mmap     ptrace 16  -> liteinst 72
close    ptrace 4   -> liteinst 72
openat   ptrace 4   -> liteinst 56
AND THE OPENED PATHS NAME THE SOURCE PRECISELY: /proc/self/maps IS OPENED 48 TIMES UNDER LITEINST AND NEVER UNDER PTRACE.
Other liteinst-only opens: libreverie_liteinst.so (2), libgcc_s.so.1 (2). ptrace opens only libc.so.6 and ld.so.cache.
48 opens of /proc/self/maps against 468 reads is ~9.75 reads per open, consistent with reading a multi-page pseudo-file to EOF.

WHY THIS FITS AN ADDITIVE OFFSET RATHER THAN A PROPORTIONAL ONE: the count is driven by a fixed number of /proc/self/maps scans, not by the guest's own workload. That is an OBSERVATION ABOUT THE DATA, NOT A MECHANISM.

AND IT GIVES THE DISCRETE VALUES A PLACE TO COME FROM: /proc/self/maps LENGTH VARIES WITH THE MAPPING COUNT, so a fixture that maps more memory needs more reads to reach EOF. {795,797,799,802} would then be read-count differences. I AM NOT ASSERTING THIS -- IT IS A TESTABLE PREDICTION AND I HAVE NOT TESTED IT.
THE TEST THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: compare read-counts against mapping-counts across the two +802 cells (fchmodat2-flags, vectored-file-io) and several +799 cells. NOT RUN.
TENTH PASS WITHOUT NAMING A CAUSE. What changed is that the observation is now specific enough for the backend owner to act on: 48 reads of /proc/self/maps to EOF per run.

COMMIT turn N, dettid 3 using resources {Path("/proc/self/maps"): R}, on previously committed <VIRTUAL TIME>

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE THREE CELLS: a virtual-time discrepancy on a preamble EVERY liteinst run performs is not fixture-specific. THE THREE KNOWN DIVERGENT CELLS MAY SIMPLY BE THE ONES WHERE IT HAPPENED TO BE OBSERVED. That is a prediction, untested.

column2: ELIMINATED 1 -- MAPS LENGTH / READ VOLUME. The two diverging runs have IDENTICAL read sequences: 235 read() calls, 107904 bytes total, and the normalised call sequences diff clean.

ELIMINATED 2 -- RCB / PERF COUNTS. The 12 rcb/retired/branch/perf lines are byte-identical between the two runs.

SCOPE, MEASURED: 34 COMMIT lines in the run; 24 of them differ. The first 9 turns AGREE EXACTLY (turn 0 at .000_000_000s, turn 1 at .000_500_000s, turn 2 at .001_544_535s in both).
DIVERGENCE BEGINS AT TURN 10, the first COMMIT whose resource is /proc/self/maps, and every later COMMIT inherits the drift.
SO: virtual time is deterministic for the first nine turns and becomes nondeterministic at the first /proc/self/maps commit, WITHOUT any difference in the syscalls, bytes, or perf counters logged.
I STILL DO NOT NAME A CAUSE. Two mechanisms are now excluded by measurement rather than by argument, which is narrower than where this pass started and is the useful part.

column1: # ROOT-CAUSE-FOUND 2026-08-15 (hermit-sabre): THE INTERMITTENT DIVERGENCE HAS A CAUSE AND IT IS STATED IN THE SOURCE, NOT INFERRED BY ME.

column2: detcore/src/scheduler.rs, at the committed_time assignment, carries this comment IN THE PRODUCT CODE:
"NB: `committed_time` still tracks the (host-timing-perturbed) global clock ... It is therefore excluded from the deterministic `--verify` comparison in `logdiff::is_scheduler_committed_time`"
SO committed_time IS KNOWN-NONDETERMINISTIC BY DESIGN, AND AN EXCLUSION EXISTS FOR IT. THE EXCLUSION IS ONE LINE WIDE:
fn is_scheduler_committed_time(line: &str) -> bool { line.contains("advancing committed_time from ") }   [logdiff.rs:438]
BUT committed_time IS PRINTED IN A SECOND PLACE THE EXCLUSION DOES NOT MATCH -- scheduler.rs:3348, the sched-step5 COMMIT line:
"COMMIT turn {}, dettid {} using resources {:?}, on previously committed {}"  <- self.committed_time

MEASURED IN THE CAPTURED LOG: 0 occurrences of the EXCLUDED phrase 'advancing committed_time from' (it is detlog_debug, absent at INFO), and 34 occurrences of the COMPARED phrase 'on previously committed'.
ALL 34 CARRY THE HOST-TIMING-PERTURBED VALUE INTO THE COMPARISON. 24 of the 34 differed in the captured divergence.
THIS EXPLAINS EVERY OBSERVATION IN THIS FILE WITHOUT ANY REMAINING GUESSWORK:
intermittent rather than constant -- it diverges only when host timing perturbs the value enough to change a printed digit;
identical syscalls, bytes and perf counters -- the guest is deterministic, only the scheduler's host-clock tracker is not;
first divergence at the first /proc/self/maps commit -- that is simply where the liteinst preamble's IO-polling retries first accumulate;
liteinst-only -- the preamble does 48 maps opens and 468 reads that ptrace never performs, giving far more retry opportunities.
NOT A FIXTURE DEFECT AND NOT A CELL PROPERTY. readdir-entries, file-backed-mmap and signalfd-create are not broken; they are where a comparator leak happened to be observed.
PROPOSAL, NOT DEPLOYED -- THIS IS CORE COMPARATOR CODE AND BELONGS TO THE OWNER: either widen is_scheduler_committed_time to cover the sched-step5 COMMIT line, or stop printing committed_time there.

WHY THIS IS NOT GOALPOST-MOVING, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: the value is documented BY THE PRODUCT as host-timing-perturbed and an exclusion for it ALREADY EXISTS. Extending an existing exclusion to a second print site of the same known-nondeterministic value is completing it, not weakening the bar.
THE CHECK THE OWNER SHOULD APPLY ANYWAY: after any such change, confirm a REAL determinism regression is still refused. I have not made the change and have not run that bracket.

column1: # EXPOSURE-QUANTIFIED 2026-08-15 (hermit-sabre): THE ROOT CAUSE PUTS MY OWN PR AT RISK AND I AM REPORTING THE NUMBER AGAINST IT.

column2: IF THE LEAK IS IN THE COMPARATOR, IT IS NOT CONFINED TO THREE CELLS. Every liteinst verify run prints 34 COMMIT lines carrying the host-timing-perturbed committed_time into the comparison, so EVERY liteinst cell is exposed.
OBSERVED RATE ACROSS EVERY liteinst --verify RUN THIS SESSION: 4 divergences in 278 runs = 1.44% per run.
enabled batch 0/92 ; waiting hardening 3/120 ; readdir-entries 0/12 ; file-backed-mmap 1/31 ; signalfd-create 0/23.
CONSEQUENCE FOR #2279, STATED AGAINST MY OWN WORK: at 1.44% per run over 23 enabled liteinst cells, THE PROBABILITY OF AT LEAST ONE RED PER FULL SUITE RUN IS ROUGHLY 28%.
That is an intermittent red on main roughly one run in four, attributable to no cell in particular, which is the hardest kind of failure to diagnose after the fact.
SO THE LANDING ADVICE CHANGES AND I AM CHANGING IT: #2279 SHOULD NOT LAND BEFORE THE COMPARATOR LEAK IS FIXED, EVEN IF A RECEIPT ARRIVES. A receipt proves one run passed; it does not bound the rate.
I spent this session preparing 23 cells to land on the next receipt. THE CORRECT CALL IS NOW TO HOLD THEM, AND THAT COSTS THE THING I HAVE BEEN OPTIMISING FOR.

THE THREE CELLS ARE RECLASSIFIED, NOT EXONERATED-AND-FORGOTTEN: readdir-entries, file-backed-mmap and signalfd-create were bucketed as intermittently divergent CELLS. The defect is not theirs. They return to qualified-and-waiting, blocked by the same comparator leak as the other 61.
HONEST LIMIT ON THE RATE: 4 events in 278 runs is a wide interval, and the 28% figure inherits that width. It is the right order of magnitude for a landing decision, not a precise forecast.

column1: # FIX-PROTOTYPED-AND-TESTED 2026-08-15 (hermit-sabre): THE PROPOSED COMPARATOR FIX IS NOW PROPOSED WITH EVIDENCE. TESTED LOCALLY, REVERTED, NOT DEPLOYED.

column2: THE ONE-LINE CHANGE, detcore/src/logdiff.rs:438 -- and note the doc comment ABOVE it already says 'the per-turn committed time echoed on each COMMIT line', so the intent was there and the predicate did not implement it:
fn is_scheduler_committed_time(line: &str) -> bool {
line.contains("advancing committed_time from ")
+       || line.contains("on previously committed ")
BOTH DIRECTIONS BRACKETED, WHICH IS WHAT I SAID I HAD NOT DONE:

REFUSE: cargo test -p hermit-detcore --lib logdiff -> 32 passed, 0 failed. Includes canonical_syscall_arg_hex_difference_compares_unequal, canonical_allocation_order_difference_compares_unequal, and first_log_divergence_reports_preceding_commit_turn_and_virtual_time. THE COMPARATOR STILL REFUSES REAL DIFFERENCES.
ACCEPT: file-backed-mmap x25 liteinst --verify with the patched binary -> matched 25, diverged 0. Its unpatched record was 2 diverged in 46.

STATISTICAL HONESTY ON THAT 25: at the observed 1.44% per-run rate, 25 clean runs is what you would expect ~70% of the time WITHOUT any fix. 25/25 IS CONSISTENT WITH THE FIX WORKING AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH IT.
THE MECHANISM IS THE STRONGER EVIDENCE, NOT THE RUN COUNT: the excluded phrase is exactly the field that differed in the captured divergence, in all 40 of the 40 dominant differing lines.
REVERTED. The scratch branch is deleted and the working tree is back on the enable branch. NOTHING WAS DEPLOYED and no PR carries this change.

WHY I STOPPED AT A PROTOTYPE: this is core comparator code. The owner decides whether excluding a second print site of a value the product already documents as host-timing-perturbed is completion or weakening. I believe it is completion and I have said why; that belief is not authority.
